guidance: Tipping is customary in the USA at sit-down restaurants.
Tipping is customary in the UK, but make sure to check your bill as sometimes restaurants will automatically add a service charge. However, you can ask for this to be removed.

By French law, a 15% service charge (service compris) is automatically included in the price of every menu item and therefore tipping is not expected. However, you can still award exceptional service with a small tip.
Tipping is expected in Germany for good service with a range between 5% to 10%.
It is not customary to leave a tip in Japan.

Tipping isn't customary or expected in Switzerland and a service charge will be normally be added to your bill. If you do have exceptional service then you can apply the round up rule to your bill or leave a 5% to 10% tip.
Tipping in Greek restaurants is optional and not mandatory, though a small gesture of appreciation is always welcome for good service.
